bull.b: Arm’s IP model can scale across many customers without the company manufacturing chips, while royalties expand as licensed designs enter production and shipment volumes grow. The combination of upfront licensing and recurring usage-based revenue supports durable operating leverage and broad market reach.

Very high gross margins, strong free cash flow and minimal leverage give Arm meaningful financial flexibility. This profile can support continued research and ecosystem investment while reducing balance-sheet pressure, allowing the company to pursue growth opportunities without relying heavily on additional debt.

Rapid data-center royalty growth and stronger-than-expected AGI CPU demand indicate that Arm is extending beyond its established mobile base into important AI infrastructure markets. Broader adoption by cloud and infrastructure customers could create additional royalty and product revenue over multiple years.

bear.b: Smartphone exposure remains a meaningful source of royalty revenue, so weaker handset conditions can moderate near-term growth across a large installed market. Lower royalty expansion may persist while memory costs pressure device economics, partially offsetting faster growth from data centers and AI.

bear.t: Supply constraints may limit AGI CPU ramp
bear.b: Demand for the AGI CPU is ahead of the original opportunity estimate, but constrained manufacturing inputs could delay customer shipments and defer revenue realization. If capacity expands slowly, Arm may be unable to convert its growing pipeline into production volumes as quickly as expected.

Moving into production silicon broadens Arm’s opportunity but initially carries materially lower gross margins than its traditional IP profile. Until scale, product mix and execution improve economics, AGI CPU growth could dilute consolidated margins and place greater importance on the longer-term margin ramp.
